precepts.why:
Solomon offered “according to the commandment of Moses”, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the solemn feasts, “three times in the year”: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles. It is the same law given in Deuteronomy 16:16: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”, and “they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” So we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

But do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves; we offer obedience. Sirach puts it plainly: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is the offering. The one who takes heed to the commandment is not coming before the Lord empty; his obedience is his peace offering. That is how Israel keeps these feasts now, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, among them: by gathering together and bringing a life that keeps the commandments.

precepts.why:
“Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before the Lord empty.”

That is the commandment of Moses Solomon kept. He offered burnt offerings on the altar he built “on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” The place the Lord chose was the house in Jerusalem, and there the three feasts were kept as written, with the priests, Levites and porters in their courses by the order of David.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: At the end of twenty years in which Solomon built the house of the Most High and his own house, he built the cities Hiram had restored to him and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Solomon went to Hamathzobah and prevailed against it, built Tadmor in the wilderness and store cities in Hamath, built Bethhoron the upper and nether as fenced cities with walls, gates, and bars, and all his store, chariot, and horsemen cities.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Israel was royalty, building whole cities across the land of Solomon's dominion, in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and wherever he desired to build.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: The people left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not of Israel, Solomon made to pay tribute, while of the children of Israel he made no bondmen but men of war, chiefs, captains, and rulers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: These nations were sons of Canaan, not Israel, and their descendants left in the land paid tribute, that is taxes, to Israel. The kingdom was so strong that other nations paid Israel, and Solomon had two hundred and fifty officers ruling over the people.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 8: Solomon's Cities, Service, and Dominion

points: Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter out of the city of David to the house he had built for her, saying his wife should not dwell in David's house because the places were holy where the ark had come.
The presence of the ark set the city of David apart as holy. Solomon would not let his wife dwell where that holiness rested.
